plates.title: BEFORE WE ASK WHAT COLOUR IS
plates.summary: Familiar primitives keep their places while colour changes their grouping. Lists climb into columns; repeated palettes carry memories the code has not stored.
plates.focus: Separate geometry, colour assignment, repetition and remembered association.
plates.footer: The vocabulary is familiar. The combinations are beginning to exceed what we first asked it to do.
panels: The parts touch in one order; colour lets you gather them in another.

Matched two stacks, each exactly FIVE parts bottom-to-top: cuboid, cube, sphere, rectangular block, hemisphere dome. Identical sizes and positions. Left ALL ochre; right THREE angular parts red and sphere/dome blue. Visitor follows red past the blue sphere. Do not add wedges to these first stacks.
A neighbour has become an input.

Two matching five-part stacks, one assigning a progression by HEIGHT, the other ochre/blue/ochre/blue/ochre from bottom to top. Simple arrows ascend between neighboring levels on alternating stack. All geometry stays identical. No animation or physics.
An array has an order. The builder makes that order climb.
Close schematic inset lists five entries 0,1,2,3,4 with arrows to the five parts stacked above one another. Visitor looks up column. Next is above in THIS arrangement, not a universal rule of arrays.
Follow the yellow through the changing silhouette.

Two fixed block/wedge stacks, each box-wedge-box-wedge-box; angular boxes red, wedges yellow. One aligned; other progressively turned and narrowed. SAME colour per corresponding piece. Visitors move around the static forms; no motor arrows.
The object has not turned.

Matched views from TWO SIDES of same fixed striped shaft under broad dark cap. Six-colour order repeats around it; cap overhead, visitor below. Panel camera positions differ; do not depict shaft spinning.
The arrangement meets something you bring.

Visitor looks at a striped monumental column, with small inset of earlier table-sized construction. Familiar forms combined into a taller crown. Associations are not printed labels or claims about an artwork's authorship; companion observes. No balance simulation or falling pieces.
